# nososim

Simulate outbreaks with changing occupancy, individual attributes, and weighted
contacts in hospitals, farms, or other structured populations.

## Installation

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("CyGei/nososim")
```

## A first outbreak

Define locations and population rules, then simulate transmission.

```{r first-outbreak}
library(nososim)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

landscape <- make_landscape(list(hospital = 30))

population <- make_population(
  landscape,
  arrivals = function(data, t) data$available,
  attributes = function(data, t) {
    data |>
      mutate(stay = sample(5:10, n(), replace = TRUE), tau = 0.2)
  }
)

dates <- as.Date("2026-01-01") + 0:20

set.seed(123)
outbreak <- make_outbreak(
  population,
  dates = dates,
  w = c(0, 0.5, 0.3, 0.2),
  imported = function(data, t) {
    if (t == dates[1]) head(data$labels, 1) else character()
  },
  contacts = function(data, t) get_contacts(data)
)

outbreak$infections |>
  count(date) |>
  ggplot(aes(date, n)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#176B65") +
  labs(x = "Infection date", y = "New cases") +
  theme_classic()
```

`stay` counts days from admission; places refill the day after departure.
`tau` sets the per-contact transmission rate. `w` gives generation-time weights
for delays 0, 1, 2, …; a leading zero prevents transmission on the infection day.

Results: `outbreak$population` holds daily snapshots before local infections
and updates; `outbreak$infections` records `from`, `to`, and `date`
(`from = NA` for imported cases).

See the [getting started guide](https://CyGei.github.io/nososim/articles/nososim.html)
for staff schedules, changing stays, and weighted contacts, or the
[function reference](https://CyGei.github.io/nososim/reference/index.html)
for arguments.
